# HEADSTART-ACS Completes Enrollment Ahead of Schedule, the Largest Heart Attack Detection Study to Date Using HeartBeam Technology


October 21, 2026 8:31am EDT[Download as PDF](https://d1io3yog0oux5.cloudfront.net/_5e8c01ff707ff63e1fad375846fb3345/heartbeam/news/2026-10-21_HEADSTART_ACS_Completes_Enrollment_Ahead_of_132.pdf)


- *HEADSTART-ACS study conducted in collaboration with Indonesia’s National Cardiovascular Center in world’s fourth most populous country, representing strategically significant market of 288 million people*
- *Data analysis is underway, with results anticipated for presentation at a cardiology conference in 2027*
- *With the HEADSTART-ACS and ALIGN-ACS studies, HeartBeam has clinical experience with more than 600 patients in heart attack detection, ahead of its U.S. pivotal study planned for Q1 2027*


SANTA CLARA, Calif.--(BUSINESS WIRE)--[HeartBeam, Inc.](https://www.heartbeam.com/) (NASDAQ: BEAT), a medical technology company focused on transforming cardiac care by providing powerful cardiac insights, today announced that the HEADSTART-ACS study, conducted at the National Cardiovascular Center Harapan Kita in Jakarta, Indonesia, has completed enrollment ahead of schedule. The study enrolled 486 patients with data analysis underway and the results anticipated to be presented at a cardiology conference in 2027.


HEADSTART-ACS is designed to evaluate the diagnostic accuracy of the HeartBeam System in detecting acute coronary syndrome (ACS), which includes heart attack. Patients presenting to the emergency department with chest pain were evaluated with both a standard 12-lead ECG and the HeartBeam 3D ECG, and results from both modalities will be compared against each patient’s final diagnosis at discharge. HeartBeam’s 3D ECG provides physicians with three-dimensional information about the heart’s electrical activity similar to a traditional 12-lead ECG, unlike smartwatches and other wearables. The credit card-sized device requires no cables or trained technicians and is designed to deliver a clinical-grade ECG outside of traditional hospital settings, extending access to cardiac assessment wherever patients are.


Dr. Iwan Dakota, internationally recognized interventional cardiologist and Director of the National Cardiovascular Center Harapan Kita, stated, “HeartBeam’s technology has the potential to save many lives. In cases of acute myocardial infarction, time to medical intervention is a critical determinant of patient survival. We welcome and strongly support the completion of this study at our hospital and look forward to its results with great interest.”


Together with the 132-patient ALIGN-ACS pilot study, whose results will be[presented at TCT 2026](https://www.tctconference.com/program-guide/145688?search=credit+card+sized) , HEADSTART-ACS brings total enrollment across HeartBeam’s heart attack detection studies to more than 600 patients. This body of work gives HeartBeam significant clinical experience with its heart attack detection technology ahead of the planned initiation of its pivotal study in the U.S. in the first quarter of 2027. The HeartBeam System is not currently cleared for heart attack detection and its use in the HEADSTART-ACS and ALIGN-ACS studies is investigational.


“Indonesia is a prime example of why heart attack assessment outside the hospital is a significant need,” said Branislav Vajdic, PhD, Founder and President of HeartBeam. “In a country of 288 million people spread across thousands of inhabited islands, many patients are unable to readily access a 12-lead ECG when symptoms start. Completing enrollment ahead of schedule reflects both the strong need and the dedication of our partners at Harapan Kita, and the data from this study will help advance our heart attack detection program worldwide.”


Indonesia represents a meaningful strategic opportunity for HeartBeam as the geography places significant strain on traditional ECG infrastructure. Standard 12-lead ECGs require trained clinical staff to conduct the test and physicians to interpret, limiting access to cardiac care for the country’s dispersed communities. HeartBeam and Indonesia’s Ministry of Health share a common vision to address this gap, potentially deploying the HeartBeam System across community health centers throughout the islands to assess patients presenting with chest pain and other cardiac conditions, and to identify those who need immediate care. Conducting the study at the National Cardiovascular Center is especially meaningful, as it oversees government hospitals across the islands and manages escalation of care from community and tertiary centers to advanced facilities equipped for intervention.


**About HeartBeam, Inc.**


HeartBeam, Inc. (NASDAQ: BEAT) is a medical technology company dedicated to transforming the detection and monitoring of critical cardiac conditions. The Company has developed the first-ever cable-free device capable of collecting ECG signals in 3D, from three non-coplanar directions, and synthesizing the signals into a 12-lead ECG. This platform technology is designed for portable devices that can be used wherever the patient is to deliver actionable heart intelligence. Physicians will be able to identify cardiac health trends and acute conditions and direct patients to the appropriate care – all outside of a medical facility, thus redefining the future of cardiac health management. HeartBeam’s 3D ECG technology received FDA clearance for arrhythmia assessment in December 2024, and the 12-Lead ECG synthesis software received FDA clearance for arrhythmia assessment in December 20251. The Company holds over 25 issued patents related to technology enablement. For additional information, visit[HeartBeam.com](https://www.heartbeam.com/) .
